title: Security review: encryption & KMS/BYOK/HSM
next_steps: Maria to send SOC 2 Type II report, ISO docs, and KMS/BYOK integration whitepaper (due 2025-11-24)
Daniel to share architecture diagram for Redwood Private + BYOK flow and sample API calls (due 2025-11-25)
Customer to schedule internal infra review and confirm whether they require HSM-backed keys or Cloud KMS (target 2025-11-28)
Set up 1-week POC to test key rotations and audit log exports (start week of 2025-12-01)
action_items: Maria Lopez - Send SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 cert, and security whitepaper - due 2025-11-24
Daniel Cho - Provide Redwood Private BYOK architecture diagram and sample KMS API integration notes - due 2025-11-25
Sara Nguyen - Share their internal KMS requirements and whether HSM is mandatory - due 2025-11-28
Liam O'Connell - Schedule POC kickoff and invite infra team - due 2025-11-27
summary: Review of encryption in transit and at rest, customer BYOK/HSM requirements, Redwood's support for customer-managed keys, key rotation, access controls, and audit logging. Agreement to share SOC2/ISO docs and architecture diagrams; plan a POC to validate integrations and audit log export flows.
transcript:
[00:00] Maria Lopez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maria from Redwood, AE on this account. We'll go through encryption and KMS today. 
[00:08] Priya Patel: Thanks Maria. I'm Priya, CISO at Finova. Joining from infra is Liam and security eng is Sara. We're mainly focused on encryption, BYOK and whether we need HSMs.
[00:20] Daniel Cho: Hi all, Daniel from Redwood engineering. I'll cover the technical flow for customer-managed keys, HSM options, and how audit logs look. 
[00:30] Liam O'Connell: Quick note — our compliance team requires proof that keys are never accessible plaintext to Redwood employees and that rotation can be customer-driven.
[00:42] Maria Lopez: Absolutely. That's the crux. We support multiple modes: hosted with Redwood-managed KMS, dedicated with customer-managed KMS via cloud provider, and Redwood Private which supports BYOK and on-prem HSM integrations.
[00:56] Sara Nguyen: When you say BYOK, do you mean we upload a key to your system, or you integrate to our KMS? We don't want key material uploaded.
[01:05] Daniel Cho: Good question. For BYOK we do not accept raw key material. We integrate with your KMS — e.g., AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault — via an API. For HSMs we support PKCS#11 wrappers and common HSM vendors like Thales. 
[01:22] Priya Patel: Is there an option for customer-managed keys in the hosted tier?
[01:27] Maria Lopez: Yes but with caveats. Hosted can be configured to use your cloud KMS for envelope encryption — we never hold the plaintext root. However for strict regulatory needs many customers opt for Redwood Private or Dedicated with VPC egress to their KMS.
[01:40] Liam O'Connell: Can you outline the envelope encryption flow? I want to see what lives on Redwood and what the KMS handles.
[01:47] Daniel Cho: Sure. High-level: data is encrypted at the application layer with a data key generated per-customer or per-shard. That data key is wrapped (encrypted) with a master key stored in the customer's KMS. Only the wrapped key is persisted in Redwood's storage. When a worker needs to decrypt, it calls the customer's KMS to unwrap the data key — depending on policy the unwrapping can be proxied through Redwood Private or via direct VPC peering.
[02:10] Sara Nguyen: So Redwood never stores the unwrapped key?
[02:14] Daniel Cho: Correct, by default we never store plaintext data keys. There are caching behaviors for performance (short-lived in-memory caches on running hosts), but those are ephemeral, rotated frequently, and subject to strict RBAC. 
[02:26] Priya Patel: How about key rotation? We need rotation without downtime and with strong audit trails.
[02:33] Daniel Cho: We support key rotation via re-wrapping: you create a new customer master key, update the KMS alias we reference, and we start encrypting new data with the new wrapping key. Old wrapped keys remain available to read by unwrapping with the previous KMS keys for a retention period. We can also run a background re-encryption job if you want to re-wrap existing data proactively. 
[02:53] Liam O'Connell: Does Redwood trigger unwrapping calls for every request? That might be high-latency.
[02:58] Daniel Cho: We implement a short-lived, in-memory cache of the unwrapped data key per process with TTLs tuned to SLOs — default 5 minutes. So not every request hits KMS. For higher security customers we can reduce the TTL. The cache is encrypted in memory and cleared on process exit. 
[03:14] Priya Patel: Audit logs — we need detailed logs showing who requested key operations, from which IP, and service account used.
[03:21] Maria Lopez: Our audit logs capture each KMS request (unwrap/authorize) including timestamp, service principal, and requestor IP when available. For Redwood Private deployments you can push logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3. For hosted we provide an export of structured audit logs via our Console and can integrate with Splunk/Datadog.
[03:41] Sara Nguyen: Do logs contain key material or anything sensitive?
[03:45] Daniel Cho: No, logs only include metadata — key id, operation, status, and request attributes. We never log actual key material or plaintext.
[03:52] Liam O'Connell: What about HSM-backed keys? Our auditor insists on FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSMs for certain keys. Can Redwood work with that?
[04:01] Daniel Cho: Yes. For Redwood Private we can integrate with HSMs that present a PKCS#11 interface. We can also support cloud HSM offerings like AWS CloudHSM. In those flows, the key material is generated and stays in the HSM; Redwood only receives cryptographic handles.
[04:18] Priya Patel: For rotations and audits, who has access to the HSM management plane? We don't want vendor ops to have key admin.
[04:25] Maria Lopez: Access controls are layered. For Redwood Private, customer-managed HSMs are in the customer's network or dedicated subnet, administered by your team. For Dedicated cloud HSMs, customer controls KMS policies and grant/revoke on the keys. Redwood engineers do not have default admin access; access is privileged and audited through our change management process when necessary. 
[04:44] Sara Nguyen: Is SAML/SSO integrated for RBAC to control who can request key unwrapping in the Console?
[04:51] Maria Lopez: Yes, RBAC integrates with SSO. You can map roles to groups (e.g., key-admin, infra, app). Only principals with the key-admin role can initiate key rotation or export logs. For programmatic access we use service accounts with scoped permissions. 
[05:03] Liam O'Connell: Data residency — our data must remain in EU. If we use hosted, can you guarantee keys and data stay in eu-west-1?
[05:11] Daniel Cho: We offer region pinning. Hosted customers can choose region and we ensure storage and KMS interactions remain in that region. For strict residency we recommend Redwood Private in a customer VPC region.
[05:24] Priya Patel: What about TLS in transit — mutual TLS or client certs for internal service-to-service?
[05:29] Daniel Cho: All transit is TLS 1.2+; we support mutual TLS for private peering and service endpoints. For managed hosted API we use bearer tokens over TLS; for Private/Dedicated we can enable mTLS.
[05:41] Maria Lopez: I'll pause — any specific regulatory constraints beyond SOC2/ISO you want us to consider?
[05:46] Priya Patel: PCI scope reduction is a goal; also GLBA and regional GDPR obligations. We need to ensure logs and encryption policies help with audits.
[05:55] Daniel Cho: We can map our audit and encryption controls to those frameworks; our SOC 2 controls cover key management procedures. We'll share the SOC 2 Type II report and a mapping doc.
[06:05] Sara Nguyen: A few technical nitty-gritty items: do you support customer KMS key policies limiting use to certain Redwood service principals? We want to enforce least privilege at KMS level.
[06:16] Daniel Cho: Yes, we provide the principal IDs that need to be added to your KMS key policy. For hosted, it's a Redwood service principal per region; for Private, it's the service account you create in your VPC. We can supply sample IAM policy JSON.
[06:29] Liam O'Connell: In the case of compromised host, can we trigger a revoke preventing further unwrapping? How quickly does that propagate?
[06:36] Daniel Cho: If you revoke the KMS grant or rotate the key, subsequent unwrap attempts will fail. Propagation is immediate on KMS side; any cached unwrapped keys in-memory will still be valid until their TTL expires. We recommend short TTLs or an explicit kill-switch endpoint that clears caches. We can add that to the POC.
[06:55] Priya Patel: Regarding the kill-switch, is that something we control or Redwood?
[06:59] Maria Lopez: For Redwood Private customers you can trigger it yourselves via API or Console. For hosted, we can expose a customer API that triggers cache invalidation and forces KMS calls.
[07:07] Sara Nguyen: Can you show an example flow for using HashiCorp Vault? Sometimes our infra uses Vault as our KMS.
[07:12] Daniel Cho: Sure, Vault supports transit secrets engine; we can call the Vault transit API to wrap and unwrap. The pattern is similar: Redwood calls your Vault endpoint over mTLS, unwraps, then uses the data key in memory. We provide a sample Terraform and Vault policy snippets.
[07:28] Priya Patel: Are there any known limitations with HSM vendors? For instance, certain HSMs don't support asymmetric wrapping?
[07:35] Daniel Cho: Some older HSMs have limited feature sets; we'll validate during onboarding. We maintain a compatibility matrix — I can share that. Common cloud HSMs and mainstream appliances (Thales, Utimaco) are supported.
[07:48] Maria Lopez: I'm going to call out a few mis-transcriptions we've seen in other calls — "KV cash" instead of "KV cache" — just as a note, testing will verify those operational terms.
[07:57] [laughter] Priya Patel: Good to know.
[08:00] Daniel Cho: On the topic of auditability, we can provide signed log bundles for a specific timeframe and S3 export with object-level checksums. Customers can configure retention and export cadence.
[08:12] Sara Nguyen: How long do you retain audit logs by default?
[08:15] Maria Lopez: Default retention is 90 days for hosted. Extended retention is available as an add-on; for Redwood Private you control retention.
[08:24] Liam O'Connell: For compliance we need the audit trail tied back to SSO identities. Are your logs correlated with ID provider assertions?
[08:32] Daniel Cho: Yes, logs include the requesting principal which can be mapped to your SSO identity via the service account or issued JWT subject. We can include the SAML/OIDC subject claim in log exports if you enable that mapping.
[08:45] Priya Patel: There's often a question about backups — encrypted backups of model cache, KV cache, and snapshots. 
[08:52] Daniel Cho: Backups are encrypted with the same envelope scheme. Snapshot keys are wrapped with the customer's KMS. For extra assurance, we can configure separate keys for backups and for live traffic.
[09:04] Sara Nguyen: Do you support hardware-backed key import so that keys never leave HSM?
[09:08] Daniel Cho: For HSM flows, yes keys are generated/imported and remain in the HSM. Redwood never imports raw key material. We can work through a key ceremony model if required.
[09:18] Liam O'Connell: About the POC: we'd like to test key rotation, cache invalidation, and exporting logs to our SIEM. Also measure latency impact of unwrapping flow.
[09:28] Maria Lopez: Great — we typically set up a short-lived POC environment in Redwood Private or Dedicated sandbox. Daniel will propose a POC plan with specific tests.
[09:36] Daniel Cho: I'll include latency benchmarks for cold unwraps vs warm cache and provide a small script to simulate traffic. We'll also provide sample logs and a dashboard.
[09:45] Priya Patel: On governance, we need to ensure Redwood's change management for key handling is auditable. Can you share your SOC2 control narrative around key access and employee access controls?
[09:55] Maria Lopez: Yes, we'll include the control narrative and where key management fits in our SOC 2 report. We'll also include our subcontractor list and the specifics for Redwood Private.
[10:05] Sara Nguyen: A small question: do you ever rotate the master key on our behalf without notice?
[10:10] Maria Lopez: No. We won't rotate customer-managed keys. We rotate Redwood-managed keys for hosted service as part of maintenance but we notify customers and provide opt-outs. For BYOK, rotation is controlled by you.
[10:22] Liam O'Connell: If we want an external attestation that Redwood engineers can't access plaintext, is there a technical way you demonstrate that?
[10:29] Daniel Cho: For customers who need that, we can produce architecture reviews, signed runbooks, and provide a limited audit where we show logs of key access and privileged operations. For the strictest customers, Redwood Private deployments are recommended because the HSM and KMS live in your environment.
[10:44] Priya Patel: Let's discuss network egress. If Redwood Private or Dedicated needs to call our KMS, what's the recommended network pattern?
[10:51] Daniel Cho: For cloud-based KMS, VPC peering or PrivateLink is common. For on-prem HSM, an IPsec site-to-site or private express route works. We'll document the required ports and endpoints.
[11:04] Maria Lopez: I'm going to share the list of documentation we'll send: SOC2 Type II report, ISO certs, KMS integration guide, HSM compatibility matrix, sample IAM policies, and a POC checklist.
[11:14] Priya Patel: Perfect. Also include a data residency statement for eu-west and how key operations are restricted to region.
[11:21] Maria Lopez: Will do. Any final technical questions?
[11:24] Sara Nguyen: One last one — how do you handle secrets in logs? We need assurance there are no creds or API keys leaked in application logs.
[11:31] Daniel Cho: We scrub secrets in logs with automated log scrubbers and have redaction policies. Sensitive fields are masked at collection time.
[11:38] Liam O'Connell: Ok that's covered.
[11:40] Maria Lopez: Alright let's recap: we'll send the SOC2/ISO docs and KMS/HSM guides, Daniel will send architecture diagrams and POC plan, customer will decide HSM vs cloud KMS and start scheduling POC. Action items noted. Anything else?
[11:54] Priya Patel: Nothing else from me. Thanks.
[11:58] Maria Lopez: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by EOD Thursday with the docs. 
[12:03] [call ends]

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present (e.g., "KV cash"), speaker labels may be slightly off in sections. The group expressed strong desire for BYOK without key export, HSM support, and robust audit log exports. Agreed on a POC to validate rotation and cache invalidation flows.
